artifacts.summary: Verdict: sapience extension's project-scoped grant of its four MCP write tools is a legitimate, deliberate narrower-than-registration-scope exception (bounds unreviewed personal-vault writes to one repo), not a standards violation; recommends amending mcp-server-ownership.md with an explicit carve-out naming this pattern rather than moving the grant to ~/.dotfiles.

memory_candidates.content: Pattern: when an MCP server is registered at user scope by infrastructure the repo cannot durably edit (e.g. a home-manager-enforced ~/.claude/settings.json reset every switch), and that owning infrastructure has already drawn a safe/unsafe tool-tier line (granting read tools broadly, withholding mutating tools), an extension MAY grant the withheld tier at this repo's own project scope instead of attempting to widen the externally-owned grant. This is a narrower-than-registration-scope carve-out, distinct from the existing 'safe/unsafe split requires enumeration' carve-out (which leaves the unsafe tier perpetually prompting everywhere): here the unsafe tier is deliberately granted, but only in the one repo that opted in. Requires explicit enumeration (never a wildcard) and docs stating the tradeoff. Worked example: sapience extension's four MCP write tools (sapience_remember/wrapup/handoff/adddoc) granted at project scope while absent from the user-scope dotfiles grant.

Technique: to verify a claim that a settings file is 'nix-enforced and reset every home-manager switch,' diff the deployed file (e.g. ~/.claude/settings.json) against the dotfiles source it's generated from (e.g. ~/.dotfiles/config/claude/settings.json) for the specific enforced keys named in the dotfiles module (e.g. modules/home/core/dotfiles.nix's enforced-key list). An exact match on those keys is direct evidence the file is reset, not merely an inference from documentation.

Insight: not every project-scope grant for a user-scope-registered server is load-bearing. The nix extension's settings-fragment.json grants mcp__nixos__nix/nix_versions at project scope, but those two tools are ALSO already granted at user scope in ~/.dotfiles/config/claude/settings.json -- so the project-scope copy is harmless duplication, not a gap-closer. Contrast with sapience, where the project-scope grant is the ONLY grant for those four tools anywhere. When auditing a scope-mismatch finding, check whether the user-scope grant already exists before concluding the narrower grant is filling a real gap.
